title: service-analytics (SQLite): the shared text-match arm emits `GLOB`, so a `$contains` / `$endsWith` / `$startsWith` comparand holding U+0000 is cut at the NUL; on the read scope a leading U+0000 widens `$contains` / `$endsWith` to every row
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**: `packages/services/service-analytics/src/text-match-sql.ts` `textMatchPredicateSql`, its `sqlite` arm (`GLOB`). Two compile faces from `references/compile-surfaces.md` share it:
- face 3, `read-scope-sql.ts` `compileScopedFilterToSql` (the RLS read side);
- face 4, `strategies/filter-normalizer.ts` `lowerAnalyticsWhere`.

Finding class **(a)**.

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`) from the out-of-scope findings of its #19999 dev (`os-dev-report` on #19999, PR #20019). The seat's at-tier reviewer confirmed it by reading (record 5821310673 on PR #20019). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

SQLite's `glob()` reads its pattern and the stored value as C strings, so each is cut at its first U+0000. This is the same mechanism #19999 fixes in `driver-sql` and the turso remote transport. The analytics compilers have their own copy of the arm, and it is not touched there.

Measured by the #19999 dev at PR #20019's head. Face 3 was executed: `compileScopedFilterToSql(…, { dialect: 'sqlite' })` ran on better-sqlite3 over the values `'a'`+U+0000+`'b'`, `'ab'`+U+0000, U+0000+`'z'`, `'plain'` and `''`:

| scope filter | rows returned | JS answer |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `$contains:` U+0000 | all 5 | 3 |
| `$endsWith:` U+0000 | all 5 | 1 |
| `$contains:` U+0000+`'b'` | all 5 | 1 |
| `$startsWith:` U+0000 | `''` and U+0000+`'z'` | 1 |

Face 4 was not executed; it shares the arm by reading.

## Why it matters

On face 3, a widening is not a loose filter. It is a read scope admitting rows its policy excludes. Whether a scope comparand can come from a value a caller controls (for example a user attribute interpolated into the scope) is NOT MEASURED. If it can, triage should weigh the `security` label.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

Reuse the constructs PR #20019 measured NUL-safe on better-sqlite3, sql.js and libSQL:
- `instr(col, ?) > 0` for `contains`;
- `instr(col, ?) = 1` for `starts`;
- a BLOB byte suffix for `ends`. Take the zero-length-value fix PR #20019 is landing: `coalesce(substr(…), X'')`, so the predicate is false, not NULL, on `''`.

Keep `GLOB` for every NUL-free comparand, byte for byte. Declare faces 3 and 4 per `references/compile-surfaces.md`.

## Filing-gate answers

- **Class**: ① (defect, named landing site); finding class (a). Face 3 was measured by execution by the dev, and the seat's reviewer confirmed the arm by reading.
- **Acting reader**: the seat that owns `packages/services/*` after triage routes it (`domain:services`). It lands after PR #20019, whose constructs and zero-length fix it reuses.
- **Dedupe**, MCP semantic issue search in this repo, `closed` included:
  - `service-analytics read scope SQL sqlite GLOB text match comparand NUL over-reach` → 10 hits, including #20018 (open; plain-object `$eq` and null-in-`$in` scope shapes), #19999 (the driver half), and the closed #15684, #15780, #13926, #5333, #6518 and #5567 (the LIKE case fold, `translate()`, `$not` over empty `$in`, the echo, the fold contract, and LIKE escaping). None covers a U+0000 comparand.
  - Control: the query reaches the analytics text-match cards.
